trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied Ruby Symbol may be written raw (as "\\" + symbol) onto the IMAP command line; at the pinned commit validate_data accepts any Symbol and send_symbol_data emits it unescaped, so CR/LF or atom-specials in a Symbol reach the socket.

landing_point.why: send_symbol_data is the only place that turns a Symbol into wire bytes; the summary ('unvalidated Symbol inputs') leads straight to it and to the empty Symbol branch of validate_data at line 27.

fix_sites.entry_point: any public command passing a Symbol arg via send_command (e.g. Net::IMAP#store/#uid_store flags, #append flags) -> validate_data
same public commands -> send_command -> send_data Symbol branch
Net::IMAP::Atom (:nodoc: internal class, no caller in lib/ at the pinned commit) gains constructor validation (fix.diff:53-63)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All fix hunks are in lib/net/imap/command_data.rb; the Atom hunk (lib/net/imap/command_data.rb:171-175) is an internal class with no caller in lib/ at the pinned commit, so it is not a reachable out-of-scope entry point.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Net::IMAP#enable interpolates its (Symbol or String) capability names straight into the command name, not through send_data, so a solver can argue 'capability names are not flag/Symbol arguments, and enable is documented as experimental/caution-advised'; RawData routes can be dismissed as documented raw-string passthrough (search string, fetch/store attr) covered by separate sibling advisories.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate system flags passed as Symbols (:Seen, :Deleted, :Flagged) must still serialize as \Seen etc. in STORE/APPEND, and Strings with specials must still be quoted/literal rather than rejected; an over-broad fix that rejects Symbols, or that rejects specials in Strings too, breaks documented usage (store(6..8, "+FLAGS", [:Deleted]); append(..., [:Seen], ...)).

O6_input_shapes: Symbol nested inside an Array argument (validate_data recurses, lib/net/imap/command_data.rb:22-24)

O7_producer.where: Response parser turns server flags into Symbols (lib/net/imap/response_parser.rb:1942-1974) which callers may feed back to #store, but they come from atom grammar so cannot carry specials; not a producer of the flaw.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Net::IMAP#enable joins caller capability names (Symbols not in ENABLE_ALIASES, or Strings) unvalidated into the command string written by put_string
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not a Symbol-as-flag argument and not via send_data; enable is documented as experimental ('Caution is advised', lib/net/imap.rb:2488).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: lib/net/imap.rb vs landing point lib/net/imap/command_data.rb (1 file away, same package)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Net::IMAP#setquota builds RawData from quota.to_s with no validation, so a non-Integer quota reaches put_string raw
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: quota is documented as a number; RawData is a different class from Symbol and likely in a sibling advisory's scope.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: String fetch attr / store attr / search, sort and thread key strings are wrapped as RawData and emitted verbatim by RawData#send_data
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Documented as raw IMAP strings (lib/net/imap.rb:2040-2042); the fix commits' raw_data-warnings merges suggest a separate advisory; RawData is not a Symbol.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: StringFormatter.string accepts Symbols and to_s's them; a variant that emits Symbols as raw atoms (for ID/metadata keys) would be a natural sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: valid_string? already treats Symbols specially (line 340-342); a maintainer optimizing to send atom-safe Symbol keys unquoted is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: normalize_searching_criteria could map Symbols in search keys to a raw keyword form (e.g. :SEEN -> SEEN) without validation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Search keywords are atoms, and Symbol-as-keyword is an idiomatic Ruby API convenience.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: #status could accept Symbol attribute names and emit them as bare atoms via a separate helper.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Status attrs are atoms (MESSAGES, UIDNEXT); a Symbol-friendly API is realistic and would sit outside command_data.rb.

O9_family: CRLF / command injection into a line-based protocol (IMAP command argument serialization)

O10_build.project_tests: test/net/imap/test_command_data.rb (FakeCommandWriter unit tests) and test/net/imap/test_imap.rb (with_fake_server in-process fake IMAP server); both run offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject only CR/LF in send_symbol_data (or validate only top-level Symbols in send_command), leaving atom-specials, nested Symbols and #enable open.

out_of_scope_notes: send_command_with_continuations writes caller block output + CRLF raw (lib/net/imap.rb:2979); SASL authenticator output, not this advisory's property.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo flag inferred from the gem being a single small library (lib/ is ~40 Ruby files).

O1 count is an enumeration of public commands that commonly carry Symbols (store, uid_store, append, search, uid_search, sort, uid_sort, thread, uid_thread, fetch, uid_fetch, status); any command arg can be a Symbol, so the true count is higher.
Diffs for merge commits aec06996 and 6bf02aef (raw_data-warnings backports) are empty in fix.diff; whether RawData routes are covered by a sibling advisory is not confirmed.
